text: Run tests with `cargo nextest run`. Doctests don't run under nextest; run them with `cargo test --doc`.
Snapshot tests use insta. Review changes with `cargo insta review`; never hand-edit .snap files.
All user-facing output goes through the Renderer trait in src/output/. Commands return data structs and never println! directly.
JSON output is a public contract: add fields only, never rename or remove them, and bump schema_version in src/output/json.rs on any change.
stdout is for data, stderr for progress and warnings. In JSON mode nothing else may reach stdout, so the output can be piped to jq.
CLI integration tests use assert_cmd against a temp repo built by tests/common/fixture_repo.rs; never depend on the developer's real git config.
Flags use clap derive only. Every new flag needs a doc comment (it becomes the --help text) and a row in the README's flag table.
User-visible changes need a line under 'Unreleased' in CHANGELOG.md; the release script fails if that section is empty.
MSRV is 1.75 (rust-version in Cargo.toml) and CI checks it; avoid language features stabilized after 1.75.
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` must pass. Fix lints instead of adding allow attributes.
Each command prints its own output with println!; there is no output abstraction yet.
Tests run with plain `cargo test`; nextest isn't set up.
The gc command shells out to `git gc --auto` because git2 has no gc API; on Windows git must be on PATH.
The Homebrew formula lives in a separate tap repo and is bumped by the release workflow; don't edit it by hand.
Deleting remote branches (`prune --remote`) needs an SSH agent; the HTTPS credential-helper path is untested on Windows.
Commits follow Conventional Commits; release-please derives the version bump from them.
The interactive picker (`gitsweep pick`) uses ratatui and sits behind the `tui` cargo feature, off by default.
The current branch and the default branch (from origin/HEAD) are always protected and must never appear as prune candidates.
JSON output isn't planned; users who need machine-readable output should parse the table with awk.
Release with `cargo release minor` from main after the release PR merges; the crates.io publish runs in CI.
User config is ~/.config/gitsweep/config.toml; protected_patterns takes globs like release/*.
Criterion benchmarks live in benches/; run `cargo bench --bench scan` before and after touching the ref scanner.
Errors: anyhow in main and commands, thiserror enums in library modules. Exit code 2 for usage errors, 1 for runtime errors.
